Looking for an adorable Thanksgiving crochet pattern that is small, colorful, and full of personality? This Mini Turkey Squish crochet pattern is a wonderful fall project for anyone who loves seasonal amigurumi and quick crochet makes.

With its round squishy body, tiny yellow feet, colorful tail feathers, cute beak, and classic turkey wattle, this little crochet turkey makes a charming addition to your Thanksgiving decorations.

Finished at approximately 4.5 inches tall and wide, excluding the feet and tail feathers, the Mini Turkey Squish is also a manageable project when you want something festive without committing to a large amigurumi.

It can be displayed on a mantel, Thanksgiving table, shelf, desk, or fall tiered tray. You could even crochet several in different color combinations and create your own little turkey family.

If you’re already planning your autumn crochet projects, you may also enjoy the Bobble Stitch Pumpkin Pattern for another cozy seasonal project.

 

About the Mini Turkey Squish Crochet Pattern

The Mini Turkey Squish is a smaller version of a traditional squishy crochet turkey design.

Instead of creating a tall amigurumi body with separate head and torso sections, the turkey is constructed using two rounded crochet pieces that are sewn together and stuffed.

The shaping creates a plump, almost pillow-like turkey.

The design includes:

  • A brown squishy body
  • Two small yellow feet
  • A yellow crochet beak
  • A red wattle
  • Five colorful tail feathers
  • Two safety eyes
  • Lightly shaped side wings
  • Soft fiberfill stuffing

The combination of brown, yellow, orange, and red gives the turkey a classic autumn look that works beautifully with Thanksgiving décor.

For even more seasonal decorating inspiration, take a look at this Fall Crochet Centerpiece Pattern.

Why You’ll Love This Crochet Turkey

There is something especially fun about small seasonal crochet projects.

They don’t require the same time commitment as a large blanket or garment, yet they still let you experiment with shaping, color changes, and amigurumi construction.

This little turkey is particularly appealing because the finished design looks detailed even though most of the body is constructed using basic crochet rounds.

It’s Small and Quick to Make

At around 4.5 inches across and tall before adding the feet and feathers, this is a relatively compact project.

That makes it ideal for:

  • Weekend crochet projects
  • Thanksgiving decorations
  • Fall craft fairs
  • Handmade gifts
  • Scrap yarn projects
  • Seasonal desk décor
  • Crochet gift baskets

It Uses Classic Fall Colors

Brown forms the main body while yellow, orange, and red create the details.

These warm colors instantly give the turkey a Thanksgiving feel.

You can follow the traditional color palette or create your own variation using mustard, rust, burgundy, cream, or even muted farmhouse shades.

The Tail Feathers Add Plenty of Character

The five dimensional tail feathers are one of the standout features of this design.

Instead of flat feather shapes, they are crocheted into small dimensional pieces and positioned in a fan across the back of the turkey.

The center feather stands upright while the surrounding feathers gradually angle outward.

This gives the Mini Turkey Squish its recognizable turkey silhouette.

Mini Turkey Squish Materials

 

Before beginning your turkey, gather all the necessary crochet supplies.

Yarn

The original project uses approximately 105 yards of bulky weight yarn.

A cotton and nylon blend works particularly well because it provides excellent stitch definition while still creating a soft finished toy.

You’ll need approximately:

Brown

About 60 yards

Brown is used for the main body and will require the largest amount of yarn.

Yellow

About 15 yards

Yellow is used for:

  • The beak
  • Feet
  • One tail feather

Orange

About 15 yards

Orange is used for two tail feathers.

Red

About 15 yards

Red is used for:

  • The wattle
  • Two tail feathers

You don’t necessarily need to use exactly these colors.

A deeper fall palette using rust, mustard, cranberry, and chocolate brown would also look beautiful.

Crochet Hook

Use a:

US H/8 – 5.0 mm crochet hook

The hook should create fabric that is firm enough to hold the stuffing without creating large gaps between stitches.

Amigurumi often benefits from slightly tighter tension than regular crochet projects.

Additional Supplies

You’ll also need:

  • Fiberfill stuffing
  • Two 14 mm safety eyes
  • Stitch markers
  • Yarn needle
  • Scissors
  • Pins for assembly

A stitch marker is especially helpful because much of the turkey’s body is crocheted continuously in a spiral.

Finished Size

The finished Mini Turkey Squish measures approximately:

4.5 inches across and 4.5 inches tall

This measurement does not include the feet or tail feathers.

Because crochet tension varies, your finished turkey may be slightly larger or smaller.

Crochet Gauge

After completing Round 3 of the body, the circle should measure approximately:

2.75 inches across

Gauge isn’t quite as critical for amigurumi as it is for fitted garments, but it can still affect the final size and the amount of yarn required.

If your piece is significantly larger than the suggested measurement, consider using a smaller hook.

If it is considerably smaller, you may need a slightly larger hook or looser tension.

Crochet Skill Level

The Mini Turkey Squish is best suited to an advanced beginner or intermediate crocheter.

Most of the body uses familiar stitches, but several techniques may be less familiar to beginners.

It helps if you already know how to:

  • Crochet in the round
  • Make a magic circle
  • Single crochet
  • Half double crochet
  • Double crochet
  • Slip stitch
  • Increase stitches
  • Decrease stitches
  • Seam crochet pieces together
  • Sew amigurumi parts securely

The project also uses linked crochet stitches and a standing double crochet technique for some of the shaping.

Don’t worry if these stitches are new to you. Practice them with scrap yarn before starting the final project.

US Crochet Abbreviations

This pattern uses US crochet terminology.

Common abbreviations include:

ch – chain
sc – single crochet
hdc – half double crochet
dc – double crochet
sl st – slip stitch
st/sts – stitch/stitches
rnd – round
rep – repeat
dc2tog – double crochet two together
ldc – linked double crochet
ltr – linked treble crochet
CSDC – chainless starting double crochet

Knowing these abbreviations before starting makes the project much easier to follow.

How the Mini Turkey Squish Is Constructed

The turkey can be divided into several small sections.

You’ll crochet:

  1. The bottom half of the body
  2. The top half of the body
  3. One beak
  4. One wattle
  5. Two feet
  6. Five tail feathers

Everything is then assembled before the turkey is stuffed and completely closed.

Crochet the Bottom Half of the Turkey Body

The turkey begins with the brown body.

Start with a magic circle and gradually increase the number of stitches during each round.

The early rounds create a flat circular shape.

Additional rounds without increases begin giving the body more depth.

Toward the outer portion of the body, taller linked stitches are strategically worked into opposite sections.

These stitches create subtle raised areas that form the turkey’s side shaping.

When the bottom section is complete, finish the round neatly and weave in the yarn end.

Set the piece aside while making the top section.

Crochet Tip

Because these rounds are worked continuously, place a stitch marker in the first stitch of every round.

Move the marker upward each time you reach it.

This simple habit can prevent a lot of counting mistakes.

Crochet the Top Half of the Turkey

 

The top half starts almost exactly like the bottom.

Begin with another brown magic circle and work the same expanding rounds.

After reaching the correct diameter, continue working even rounds before adding the side shaping.

This second section becomes the turkey’s face and upper body.

Leave a long yarn tail when finishing because this yarn will later be used to sew the two body sections together.

Don’t join the body halves yet.

The eyes, feathers, feet, wattle, and beak need to be positioned first.

Crochet the Turkey Beak

The tiny beak requires only a small amount of yellow yarn.

It is created with a short chain and several stitches worked into the same chain space.

The resulting shape forms a small pointed beak.

Leave a generous yarn tail after finishing.

You’ll use this tail to attach the beak securely between the eyes during assembly.

Crochet the Turkey Wattle

No Thanksgiving turkey would be complete without its distinctive red wattle.

The wattle is made with a short foundation chain followed by progressively shorter stitches.

Using different stitch heights naturally creates the tapered shape.

Leave another long sewing tail when finishing.

The wattle sits slightly below and beside the beak on the finished turkey.

Crochet the Turkey Feet

 

Make two yellow feet.

The feet begin with chains that form the legs.

Additional chains and stitches create the little toes.

Although the construction may feel unusual when you’re making the first foot, the shape becomes much clearer once it is attached to the body.

Remember that the two feet should mirror one another.

Before sewing, flip one foot so the toes naturally point in corresponding directions.

Crochet the Turkey Tail Feathers

Now comes one of the most enjoyable parts of this Thanksgiving crochet pattern: the colorful turkey feathers.

You’ll make five feathers total:

  • 1 yellow feather
  • 2 orange feathers
  • 2 red feathers

Each feather begins with a small circular base.

The rounds are then worked upward to create a slightly tubular, rounded feather.

Decreases near the top narrow the shape.

Finally, the remaining stitches are cinched closed.

Leave yarn tails for sewing each feather onto the body.

Arranging the Tail Feathers

 

 

The feather arrangement is important because it creates the recognizable fan-shaped turkey tail.

Place the yellow feather vertically in the center.

Position one orange feather on either side.

Finally, place the two red feathers toward the outside edges.

Your arrangement should look roughly like this:

Red – Orange – Yellow – Orange – Red

Angle the outside feathers slightly farther outward.

Before sewing, pin all five feathers into place.

Look at the turkey from both the front and back to make sure the feather fan looks balanced.

Then sew each feather securely.

Adding the Safety Eyes

Position the two safety eyes on the front half of the turkey.

They should sit evenly between the side shaping.

Before attaching the washers permanently, check:

  • Eye spacing
  • Beak placement
  • Wattle position
  • Overall facial balance

Once you’re happy with the face, secure the safety eye backs.

Safety Note

Safety eyes contain small pieces and may not be appropriate for toys intended for babies or children under three.

If making the turkey for a young child, embroidered eyes can be a safer alternative.

Mini Turkey Squish Assembly

Assembly is where all those little crochet pieces finally begin looking like a turkey.

Take your time during this stage.

Step 1: Position the Eyes

Attach the safety eyes to the top body section.

Make sure they are evenly spaced and centered on the front.

Step 2: Add the Feet

Sew the two yellow feet onto the bottom body section.

Allow the toes to remain loose so they extend naturally from the body.

Step 3: Attach the Wattle

Position the red wattle near the center front of the turkey.

It should sit underneath the area where the beak will eventually be attached.

Step 4: Sew on the Tail Feathers

Attach all five tail feathers to the back of the top body section.

Keep the yellow feather centered and distribute the orange and red feathers evenly on either side.

Step 5: Join the Body Pieces

Place the top and bottom body sections together.

Use the long yarn tail to whip stitch around the edge.

Sew a little more than halfway around before stopping.

Leave enough room to add stuffing.

Step 6: Attach the Beak

Sew the yellow beak between the eyes.

Position it just above the wattle.

Check that the face looks centered before fastening the yarn securely.

Step 7: Stuff the Turkey

 

Add fiberfill gradually.

Don’t push one large handful into the body at once.

Instead, add small amounts and distribute the stuffing evenly.

This helps maintain the turkey’s rounded shape.

Step 8: Finish Closing

Continue whip stitching around the remaining opening.

Before closing the last few stitches, adjust the stuffing if necessary.

Fasten securely and weave the remaining yarn tail into the body.

Your Mini Turkey Squish is complete!

Tips for a Neater Crochet Turkey

Small details can make a big difference when making amigurumi.

Keep Your Tension Consistent

The body should be crocheted firmly enough that the stuffing isn’t visible between stitches.

Don’t Overstuff

Too much fiberfill can stretch the stitches and distort the round turkey shape.

Add enough stuffing to make the turkey plump while keeping the crochet fabric smooth.

Pin Everything Before Sewing

Before permanently attaching the beak, feathers, feet, or wattle, pin them into position.

Look at the turkey from several angles.

Small placement adjustments can dramatically improve the finished appearance.

Leave Long Sewing Tails

When finishing small pieces, resist the temptation to cut the yarn short.

Long tails make assembly much easier.

Secure the Feathers Well

The feathers are dimensional pieces that may receive more handling than flat appliqués.

Sew around the base several times so they remain firmly attached.

Color Ideas for Your Crochet Turkey

Traditional Thanksgiving colors look wonderful, but there is no reason every turkey has to look the same.

Try one of these palettes.

Traditional Thanksgiving Turkey

  • Chocolate brown
  • Mustard yellow
  • Pumpkin orange
  • Cranberry red

Farmhouse Turkey

  • Taupe
  • Cream
  • Muted mustard
  • Terracotta

Pastel Turkey

  • Beige
  • Dusty pink
  • Peach
  • Soft yellow

Woodland Turkey

  • Dark brown
  • Olive green
  • Rust
  • Gold

Colorful Turkey

Use leftover yarn and make every feather a different color.

This is an especially fun option for scrap yarn projects.

How to Use Your Mini Crochet Turkey

Once finished, there are plenty of ways to display your little turkey.

Thanksgiving Table Decoration

Place one at each end of your Thanksgiving table or make several for a larger centerpiece.

For a complete handmade display, pair your turkey with this Fall Crochet Centerpiece Pattern.

Fall Shelf Décor

Add your turkey to a seasonal shelf alongside pumpkins, leaves, and other crochet decorations.

The Bobble Stitch Pumpkin Pattern makes a natural companion project.

Handmade Thanksgiving Gift

A tiny crochet turkey makes a thoughtful seasonal gift for friends, teachers, hosts, or family members.

Craft Fair Item

Small seasonal amigurumi projects can also make eye-catching additions to autumn craft displays.

Kids’ Thanksgiving Décor

Embroider the eyes instead of using safety eyes when making decorations intended for younger children.

More Fall Crochet Patterns

If you’re building your autumn crochet collection, don’t stop with the turkey.

Bobble Stitch Pumpkin

Nothing says autumn quite like crochet pumpkins.

Try the Bobble Stitch Pumpkin Pattern for a textured pumpkin that pairs beautifully with the turkey.

Fall Crochet Centerpiece

Create an entire handmade seasonal display with this Fall Crochet Centerpiece Pattern.

It’s a great project to combine with your crochet pumpkins and turkey for Thanksgiving decorating.

Crochet Pumpkin Bear

If cute amigurumi is your favorite type of project, you’ll also love the Crochet Pumpkin Bear Pattern.

The pumpkin theme makes it ideal for your fall crochet project list.

Crochet Pumpkin Beanie

Looking for something wearable?

Try this adorable Crochet Pumpkin Beanie Pattern for another fun autumn project.

Mini Turkey Squish Crochet Pattern FAQ

What size is the Mini Turkey Squish?

The finished turkey measures approximately 4.5 inches across and 4.5 inches tall, not including the tail feathers and feet.

What yarn weight works best?

The original design uses bulky weight #5 yarn.

Using a different yarn weight will change the finished size.

What crochet hook size should I use?

A 5.0 mm US H crochet hook is recommended.

You can adjust the hook size slightly depending on your natural tension and chosen yarn.

Is this crochet turkey beginner friendly?

An adventurous beginner who is comfortable crocheting in the round may be able to make it, but some construction methods and special stitches make the pattern better suited to an advanced beginner or intermediate crocheter.

Can I use leftover yarn?

Absolutely.

The beak, feet, wattle, and individual feathers use relatively small amounts of yarn, making this an excellent project for using leftover autumn-colored yarn.

Can I make the turkey larger?

Yes.

Using thicker yarn and a larger crochet hook will naturally produce a larger turkey.

Just remember that you’ll also need more stuffing and yarn.

Can I use embroidered eyes instead of safety eyes?

Yes.

Embroidered eyes are an excellent alternative, particularly if you’re making the turkey for a baby or toddler.

How many tail feathers does the turkey have?

The Mini Turkey Squish uses five crochet tail feathers.

The suggested layout is one center yellow feather, two orange feathers, and two red outer feathers.

A Fun Thanksgiving Crochet Project

The Mini Turkey Squish crochet pattern combines everything that makes seasonal amigurumi fun: warm fall colors, an adorable expression, dimensional details, and a relatively small finished size.

The plump body makes the turkey wonderfully squishy, while the colorful feather fan gives it plenty of Thanksgiving character.

Whether you’re making one for your own autumn décor, adding handmade pieces to your Thanksgiving table, preparing small seasonal gifts, or simply looking for your next cute crochet project, this tiny turkey is a fun way to celebrate fall with yarn and a crochet hook.

And if you’re planning a full collection of autumn projects, pair your turkey with the Bobble Stitch Pumpkin, Crochet Pumpkin Bear, or Fall Crochet Centerpiece for a coordinated handmade fall display.

Happy crocheting and enjoy creating your own little Thanksgiving turkey!

title.rendered: Bohemian Style Wrap Bracelet with Beads Tutorial

content.rendered:
If you love relaxed, layered jewelry, this bohemian wrap bracelet with beads is a simple handmade project that combines seed beads, leather or waxed cotton cord, and a button closure.

The bracelet wraps around the wrist two or three times, giving it that classic boho look without requiring advanced jewelry-making skills. Once you understand the beading sequence, the method is repetitive and easy to customize with different bead colors, cord types, and button styles.

Why You’ll Love This Boho Wrap Bracelet

This project is:

  • beginner-friendly
  • easy to personalize
  • lightweight and comfortable
  • perfect for stacking
  • ideal for friendship bracelets and handmade gifts
  • easy to adapt with different beads and cord colors

You can keep the design neutral and earthy or make it brighter with colorful seed beads.

Materials

You will need:

  • glass seed beads or larger beads if using thicker cord
  • leather cord or waxed cotton cord, around 1 mm
  • button for the closure
  • strong polyester sewing thread in a color that coordinates with the cord

Equipment

You will also need:

  • clipboard or a piece of cardboard with a paper clamp, optional
  • thin needle
  • scissors

How to Make a Bohemian Style Wrap Bracelet with Beads

 

 

Step 1: Measure and Cut the Cord

Start by measuring around your wrist.

The cord should be long enough to wrap around your wrist at least two or three times, plus about 3 cm extra for the closure.

Then double that amount because the bracelet uses the cord folded in half.

It is better to cut a little extra than to end up short.

Step 2: Fold the Cord and Make the Closure Loop

Fold the cord in half.

At the folded end, create a loop large enough for your button to pass through.

Tie a knot directly below the loop to secure it.

This loop will become one side of the bracelet closure.

Before tightening completely, check that the button can pass through the loop without being too loose.

Step 3: Secure the Bracelet to Your Work Surface

If you are using a clipboard, clamp the loop under the clip.

You can also secure the bracelet to a piece of cardboard with a paper clamp.

The two cord strands should hang straight downward.

Keeping the bracelet secure makes it much easier to maintain even tension while adding the beads.

Step 4: Attach the Beading Thread

Tie the sewing thread onto the right cord.

Leave a fairly long thread tail.

Do not trim it yet because you will use this loose end later to secure the beginning of the bracelet.

Thread your needle onto the working thread.

You are now ready to begin adding beads.

Step 5: Add the First Seed Bead

Pick up one seed bead with the needle.

Position the bead between the two cord strands.

To secure it, follow this thread path:

  1. Pass the thread under the right cord.
  2. Pass the needle through the bead.
  3. Bring the thread over the left cord.
  4. Now reverse the direction.
  5. Pass the thread under the left cord.
  6. Go back through the same bead.
  7. Bring the thread over the right cord.

Repeat this process until the thread has passed through the bead a total of four times — twice in each direction.

This secures the bead firmly between the two cords.

Step 6: Continue Adding Beads

Pick up the next bead.

Position it directly below the first bead.

Repeat the same stitching process:

  • under one cord
  • through the bead
  • over the opposite cord
  • reverse direction
  • pass back through the bead

Continue adding beads one at a time.

As the bracelet grows, the beads should form a neat row between the two outer cords.

Keep working until the bracelet reaches the length you need for two or three wraps around your wrist.

Keep the Beadwork Even

Try to maintain consistent tension throughout the bracelet.

If the thread is too loose, the beads may shift.

If it is too tight, the cords may pull inward.

A neat bracelet should have:

  • evenly spaced beads
  • straight outer cords
  • consistent tension
  • a flexible feel

Check the bracelet against your wrist occasionally as you work.

Step 7: Secure the Working Thread

When the bracelet has reached the desired length, tie off the working thread.

Then pass the needle back through approximately three beads.

This helps secure the thread end inside the beadwork.

Once the thread feels stable, trim off the excess.

Step 8: Add the Button Closure

Tie a knot in the two cord ends near the final bead.

Slide the button onto the cords.

Then tie another knot below the button to hold it securely in place.

Trim the cords, leaving approximately 3 cm beyond the button knot.

The button should fit easily through the loop you created at the beginning.

Step 9: Finish the Cord Ends

Tie a small knot at the end of each loose cord.

These knots help keep the ends neat and reduce the chance of the cord unraveling.

Trim any excess if necessary.

Step 10: Secure the Beginning Thread Tail

Return to the long loose thread tail you left at the beginning of the bracelet.

Thread it through the needle.

Pass it back through a few beads several times to secure it.

Trim the excess thread.

Your bohemian wrap bracelet is now finished.

How the Beading Technique Works

The bead sits between two parallel cords.

The sewing thread travels:

under one cord → through the bead → over the other cord

and then returns in the opposite direction.

Repeating this several times locks the bead in place.

The result is a row of beads framed by two cords.

Choosing Beads for a Boho Bracelet

You can use many different bead styles.

Good options include:

  • glass seed beads
  • metallic seed beads
  • matte beads
  • faceted beads
  • gemstone beads
  • wooden beads
  • ceramic beads

If you use thicker cord, choose beads with larger holes.

Bohemian Color Ideas

For a classic earthy look, try:

  • turquoise and brown
  • cream and bronze
  • amber and tan
  • black and gold
  • olive green and beige

For something brighter:

  • coral and turquoise
  • rainbow beads
  • pink and gold
  • blue and silver
  • purple and cream

How Long Should a Wrap Bracelet Be?

The finished bracelet should wrap comfortably around your wrist two or three times.

The exact length depends on:

  • wrist size
  • cord thickness
  • bead size
  • desired number of wraps

Measure around your wrist first and check the fit as you work.

Tips for a Neat Boho Wrap Bracelet

Keep the Cord Tension Even

The two outer cords should stay parallel.

Avoid pulling one side tighter than the other.

Secure the First Beads Carefully

The first few beads set the alignment for the rest of the bracelet.

Take your time at the beginning.

Check the Button Loop

Before finishing the bracelet, confirm that the button fits through the closure loop.

It should pass through securely without being too loose.

Use Strong Thread

The thread passes through each bead multiple times, so strong polyester sewing thread is a good choice.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this wrap bracelet beginner-friendly?

Yes. The main technique is repetitive and becomes easier after the first few beads.

What size cord should I use?

The original version uses approximately 1 mm leather or waxed cotton cord.

How many times should the thread pass through each bead?

Pass through each bead a total of four times — twice in each direction.

Can I use larger beads?

Yes. If you use thicker cord, larger beads may work better because they usually have larger holes.

How does the bracelet close?

A loop is created at one end and a button is attached at the other.

The button passes through the loop to secure the bracelet.

Can I make a single-wrap version?

Yes. Simply shorten the bracelet so it wraps around the wrist once instead of two or three times.

Quick Pattern Summary

  1. Measure the cord for two or three wraps.
  2. Add 3 cm for the closure and double the length.
  3. Fold the cord in half.
  4. Create a button loop.
  5. Secure the bracelet to a clipboard.
  6. Tie the thread to the right cord.
  7. Add the first bead.
  8. Stitch through it four times.
  9. Continue adding beads.
  10. Work until the bracelet reaches the desired length.
  11. Tie off the thread.
  12. Weave the thread through three beads.
  13. Add the button.
  14. Tie the button securely.
  15. Trim the cords, leaving about 3 cm.
  16. Tie small knots at the cord ends.
  17. Secure the beginning thread tail.
  18. Trim and wear your bracelet.

Make Your Own Bohemian Wrap Bracelet

This bohemian style wrap bracelet with beads is a simple way to create handmade jewelry with a layered, relaxed look.

The basic technique can be reused with many different beads and color combinations, so once you understand the method, you can make several versions that look completely different.

It is a great project for friendship gifts, summer jewelry, festival-inspired accessories, or simply adding a handmade boho piece to your own collection.

title.rendered: DIY Gemstone Friendship Bracelet Tutorial

content.rendered:
If you love simple handmade jewelry with a more polished look, this DIY gemstone friendship bracelet is a beautiful project to try. It combines delicate gemstone beads with gold-toned jewelry wire, crimps, and a small clasp to create a bracelet that feels minimal, elegant, and easy to personalize.

The design is especially nice because the gemstones remain the focal point. You can use just a few beads for a delicate bracelet, or add more for a bolder look.

This tutorial uses three ruby rondelle beads, but you can substitute your favorite gemstones to match a birthstone, favorite color, or the meaning you want the bracelet to represent.

Photo credit: Kernowcraft.com

Why You’ll Love This Gemstone Bracelet

This project is:

  • simple and elegant
  • easy to customize
  • quick to make
  • suitable for beginners
  • perfect for meaningful gifts
  • easy to adapt with different gemstone beads

The bracelet uses a basic crimp-and-clasp technique, so once you understand the first loop, the second side follows almost the same process.

Supplies Needed

You will need:

  • gemstone beads of your choice
  • 0.45 mm gold-plated jewelry wire
  • small carabiner or lobster clasp
  • 2 gold-filled crimps, approximately 2 x 2 mm
  • snipe nose pliers or crimping pliers
  • side cutters

For the example bracelet, three small ruby rondelle beads are used.

Choosing Your Gemstone Beads

You can use almost any small gemstone beads that fit comfortably on your chosen wire.

Popular choices include:

  • ruby
  • amethyst
  • rose quartz
  • turquoise
  • garnet
  • moonstone
  • aquamarine
  • citrine

You can also choose gemstones based on birth months or simply use colors you love.

How to Make a DIY Gemstone Friendship Bracelet

Step 1: Gather Your Supplies

Before you begin, lay out everything you need.

Place your:

  • gemstone beads
  • wire
  • crimps
  • clasp
  • pliers
  • side cutters

within easy reach.

Organizing the supplies first makes the project much easier and prevents you from searching for small findings halfway through the bracelet.

Step 2: Measure and Cut the Wire

Wrap the jewelry wire around your wrist to estimate the bracelet length.

Leave a few extra centimeters of wire for making the loops and attaching the clasp.

Cut the wire using side cutters.

It is better to leave slightly too much wire than too little because the extra length gives you more room to work with the crimps.

Step 3: Add the Gemstone Beads

Thread your chosen gemstone beads onto the jewelry wire.

The example uses three ruby rondelle beads.

You can use:

  • one gemstone bead
  • three gemstone beads
  • five gemstones
  • or as many as you like

For a minimalist bracelet, three small beads in the center creates a clean, balanced look.

Step 4: Center the Beads and Add the First Crimp

Slide the gemstone beads to the middle of the wire.

Once they are centered, thread one crimp onto one end of the wire.

Move the crimp down the wire, leaving several centimeters of working space at the end.

Do not close the crimp yet.

Step 5: Create the First Loop

Take the end of the wire and bend it back toward the crimp.

Pass the wire end back through the crimp.

This creates a loop.

At first, the loop may be larger than you want.

Gently pull the wire tail to reduce the size.

Make sure the loop is still large enough to connect easily to the clasp.

Step 6: Secure the First Crimp

Once the loop is the correct size, use snipe nose pliers or crimping pliers to close the crimp.

Pinch it firmly around the wire.

The crimp should hold the loop securely in place.

Check that the loop does not slip before moving to the next step.

Step 7: Trim the Excess Wire

Use your side cutters to remove the extra wire extending beyond the crimp.

Trim carefully and as close to the crimp as practical.

Your first end is now finished.

Step 8: Add the Second Crimp and Clasp

Move to the opposite end of the bracelet.

Thread the second crimp onto the wire.

Then add your small clasp.

A lobster or carabiner-style clasp works well for this design.

Keep both pieces close to the end of the wire while you prepare the second loop.

Step 9: Create the Second Loop

Bend the wire back toward the crimp.

Pass the wire end through the crimp again, just as you did on the first side.

This forms another loop.

The clasp should sit inside this loop.

Do not tighten the crimp yet.

Step 10: Adjust and Close the Second Loop

Adjust the loop until it is the right size.

You want it snug enough to look tidy but loose enough for the clasp to move comfortably.

Use snipe nose pliers or crimping pliers to close the crimp securely.

Check that the clasp is held firmly in place.

Step 11: Trim the Remaining Wire

Use side cutters to trim away the remaining wire tail.

Cut carefully so you do not damage the clasp or crimp.

Your bracelet is now complete.

Finished Gemstone Friendship Bracelet

Your DIY gemstone friendship bracelet is ready to wear.

The finished bracelet should have:

  • a small gemstone section centered on the wire
  • a neat loop on one side
  • a clasp on the other
  • securely closed crimps
  • no sharp wire ends

This minimalist design is easy to wear alone or stacked with other bracelets.

Gemstone Bracelet Color Ideas

You can create many different versions of this bracelet by changing the gemstones.

Ruby Bracelet

Ruby gives the bracelet a rich red accent.

It works well with gold-toned wire for a warm, elegant finish.

Rose Quartz Bracelet

Soft pink rose quartz creates a delicate, romantic look.

Amethyst Bracelet

Purple amethyst adds a colorful accent and pairs nicely with either gold or silver findings.

Turquoise Bracelet

Turquoise creates a brighter, more casual friendship bracelet style.

Mixed Gemstone Bracelet

You can also combine different gemstones.

For example:

  • ruby + moonstone
  • amethyst + rose quartz
  • turquoise + citrine

Just make sure the beads are similar in size so the bracelet remains balanced.

Tips for a Neat Gemstone Bracelet

Measure Before Cutting

Leave extra wire when cutting.

You can always trim excess later, but you cannot add length once the wire is too short.

Center the Beads Before Crimping

Before closing the first crimp, make sure your gemstone beads are positioned where you want them.

Once both ends are finished, adjusting the center section becomes much more difficult.

Keep the Loops Small and Neat

The loops should be large enough for the clasp to move freely but not so large that they look oversized.

Close the Crimps Firmly

The crimps are what hold the bracelet together.

Make sure they are fully closed around the wire.

Trim Sharp Ends Carefully

Inspect both ends of the bracelet after trimming.

There should be no sharp wire ends sticking out.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this gemstone bracelet beginner-friendly?

Yes. This is a simple jewelry project because it only requires basic stringing, looping, crimping, and trimming.

How many gemstone beads should I use?

The example uses three gemstone beads, but you can use as many as you like.

For a minimalist bracelet, one to five beads works especially well.

What wire should I use?

The original project uses 0.45 mm flexible jewelry wire.

Choose a wire that is strong enough for bracelet making and flexible enough to work through crimps.

Do I need crimping pliers?

Crimping pliers are ideal, but snipe nose pliers can also be used to close the crimps.

Can I use different clasps?

Yes.

A small lobster or carabiner clasp works well, but other jewelry clasps can be used if they fit the wire loop.

Can I make this bracelet with silver findings?

Yes.

You can substitute silver-toned wire, crimps, and clasps for a cooler-toned version.

Quick Gemstone Friendship Bracelet Summary

  1. Gather all supplies.
  2. Measure the jewelry wire around your wrist.
  3. Leave extra wire and cut.
  4. Thread the gemstone beads.
  5. Center the beads.
  6. Add the first crimp.
  7. Form a loop.
  8. Close the crimp.
  9. Trim the excess wire.
  10. Add the second crimp and clasp.
  11. Form the second loop.
  12. Close the second crimp.
  13. Trim the remaining wire.
  14. Check the bracelet for sharp ends.
  15. Test the clasp.
  16. Wear and enjoy your finished bracelet.

Make Your Own DIY Gemstone Friendship Bracelet

This DIY gemstone friendship bracelet is a simple way to create handmade jewelry that feels personal and polished.

The design is easy to customize with different gemstones, metal colors, and bead counts, making it ideal for birthstone bracelets, friendship gifts, or everyday jewelry.

Once you learn how to create the crimped loops and attach the clasp, you can use the same basic technique for many other gemstone and wire bracelet designs.

Photos credit: Kernowcraft.com

title.rendered: Fruit Seed Bead Bracelet Tutorial: Easy DIY Cherry Bracelet

content.rendered:
If you love colorful handmade jewelry, these fruit seed bead bracelets are a fun and easy project to try. This design uses small seed beads to create tiny cherry motifs separated by simple spacer beads, giving the bracelet a playful summer look.

The pattern is beginner-friendly and only requires a few basic jewelry-making supplies. Once you understand how the cherry section is formed, you can repeat it around the bracelet and customize the colors however you like.

You can make these as friendship bracelets, party favors, handmade gifts, or a quick weekend craft.

Why You’ll Love This Seed Bead Bracelet

This project is:

  • easy to customize
  • beginner-friendly
  • colorful and lightweight
  • quick to make
  • perfect for friendship bracelets
  • easy to adapt into different fruit colors

The cherry pattern is especially simple because it only uses three beads for each fruit section: one green bead and two red beads.

Supplies Needed to Make Fruit Seed Bead Bracelets

You will need:

  • seed beads
  • jewelry cord
  • beading needle
  • jewelry glue
  • scissors

A lighter-weight cord may work better for forming the cherry details, especially if a thicker bracelet cord feels difficult to pass through the beads more than once.

Choosing Seed Beads

You can use one main color for the spacer beads and separate colors for the fruit motif.

For a cherry bracelet, use:

  • red beads for the cherries
  • green beads for the leaves or stem area
  • any color you like for spacer beads

Good spacer colors include:

  • white
  • pink
  • clear
  • pale yellow
  • light blue
  • cream

How to Make a Fruit Seed Bead Bracelet

Step 1: Cut the Jewelry Cord

Cut a piece of jewelry cord that is about 3 to 5 inches longer than the amount you would normally use for a bracelet.

The extra length gives you room to knot the bracelet and work comfortably.

String one bead near the end of the cord and tie it off temporarily.

This helps prevent the remaining beads from sliding off while you work.

Step 2: Add the Spacer Beads

 

 

Thread the jewelry cord through your needle.

String on your first group of spacer beads.

A good starting point is around 5 to 7 spacer beads.

These beads create space between each fruit motif.

You can use the same number each time for a consistent pattern.

Step 3: Add the Cherry Beads

 

 

After the spacer beads, string on:

  • 1 green bead
  • 2 red beads

These three beads will form the small cherry detail.

Keep them close together before moving to the next step.

Step 4: Create the Cherry Shape

 

 

Take the needle and thread it back through the green bead.

Do not pass it back through the two red beads.

Pull the needle and cord through until the thread becomes taut.

As you tighten, the two red beads should sit together beneath the green bead, forming a small cherry-like cluster.

Adjust the beads gently with your fingers if needed.

This is the key step that creates the fruit shape.

Step 5: Repeat the Pattern

Add another group of 5 to 7 spacer beads.

Then repeat the cherry sequence:

  1. add 1 green bead
  2. add 2 red beads
  3. pass the needle back through the green bead
  4. pull the cord snug

Continue alternating:

spacer beads → cherry motif → spacer beads → cherry motif

Repeat until the bracelet reaches the desired length.

Check the fit around your wrist as you work.

Step 6: Tie and Finish the Bracelet

 

 

Once the bracelet is long enough, bring the two cord ends together.

Tie them securely using a double knot.

Apply a small amount of jewelry glue or clear nail polish to the knot to help keep it from slipping.

Allow it to dry.

Then trim the excess cord with scissors.

Your fruit seed bead bracelet is finished.

How the Cherry Pattern Works

The cherry motif is made from:

  • one green bead
  • two red beads

The two red beads are added first after the green bead.

Then the needle passes back through the green bead.

When the cord is tightened, the green bead sits above the two red beads, making the cluster look like a tiny pair of cherries.

This small repeated detail is what gives the bracelet its fruit theme.

Seed Bead Bracelet Color Ideas

You do not have to stick with red and green.

You can adapt the same basic structure into different fruit-inspired combinations.

Strawberry-Inspired

Try:

  • red
  • green
  • white spacer beads

Lemon-Inspired

Use:

  • yellow
  • green
  • white or clear spacer beads

Blueberry-Inspired

Try:

  • blue
  • green
  • pale purple spacers

Watermelon-Inspired

Use:

  • pink
  • green
  • black accent beads

The basic bracelet structure stays the same.

How Many Spacer Beads Should You Use?

The original method uses about 5 to 7 spacer beads between each fruit motif.

Using fewer spacer beads creates:

  • more fruit motifs
  • a busier bracelet
  • a denser pattern

Using more spacer beads creates:

  • more breathing room
  • fewer fruit motifs
  • a simpler appearance

For a balanced design, 5 to 7 spacers works well.

Tips for a Neat Seed Bead Bracelet

Keep the Cord Tension Even

Pull the cord snug enough that the cherry motif keeps its shape, but not so tight that the bracelet begins to curl.

Check the Fit Often

Seed bead bracelets can grow quickly.

Wrap the bracelet around your wrist occasionally so you do not make it too long.

Use a Fine Enough Needle

The needle must be able to pass through the seed beads comfortably.

It also needs to fit through the green bead more than once when forming the cherry cluster.

Keep the Knot Secure

A double knot plus a small amount of jewelry glue or clear nail polish helps prevent the bracelet from coming undone.

Frequently Asked Questions

What size seed beads are best for bracelets?

Good seed bead sizes for bracelets include 6/0, 8/0, and 11/0.

For beginners, 6/0 or 8/0 beads are often easier to handle because they are larger and easier to thread.

11/0 seed beads are smaller and better for more delicate or detailed designs.

For fruit seed bead bracelets, larger beads can make the pattern easier to see.

What string should I use for seed bead bracelets?

A jewelry cord that is strong enough for bracelet use works well.

For easy on-and-off bracelets, stretch cord in the approximate 0.5 mm to 0.8 mm range can be a practical choice.

If you are making detailed fruit shapes, a lighter cord may be easier to pass through small beads multiple times.

How do you keep seed bead bracelets from coming undone?

Tie the ends in a secure double knot.

Then add a small amount of jewelry glue or clear nail polish to the knot.

Let it dry before trimming the cord.

Can beginners make this bracelet?

Yes.

This is a simple pattern because the main sequence repeats:

  • spacer beads
  • one green bead
  • two red beads
  • pass back through the green bead

Once you complete the first fruit motif, the rest of the bracelet follows the same method.

Can I make this bracelet without a needle?

It may be possible depending on the stiffness of your cord and the size of the bead holes, but a beading needle makes the process much easier.

Can I use different fruit colors?

Yes.

You can change the bead colors to create different fruit-inspired bracelets while keeping the same basic technique.

Quick Fruit Seed Bead Bracelet Pattern

For easy reference:

  1. Cut the jewelry cord 3 to 5 inches longer than your normal bracelet length.
  2. Secure one bead near the end.
  3. Add 5 to 7 spacer beads.
  4. Add 1 green bead.
  5. Add 2 red beads.
  6. Pass the needle back through the green bead.
  7. Pull the cord taut.
  8. Add another group of spacer beads.
  9. Repeat the fruit pattern.
  10. Continue until the bracelet fits.
  11. Tie the ends with a double knot.
  12. Add a small amount of glue or clear nail polish.
  13. Let it dry.
  14. Trim the excess cord.

Make Your Own Fruit Seed Bead Bracelet

This fruit seed bead bracelet is a simple way to turn basic beads into a playful handmade design.

The repeating cherry motif is easy to learn, and changing the spacer colors gives you plenty of ways to personalize the bracelet.

Once you understand the technique, you can experiment with different fruits, seed bead sizes, color combinations, and bracelet lengths to create your own collection of colorful beaded jewelry.

title.rendered: 15 Free Crochet Bag Patterns You’ll Want to Make

content.rendered:

Toggle

Looking for a stylish crochet bag pattern to add to your project list? You’re in the right place. This collection brings together 15 beautiful free crochet bag patterns, including roomy tote bags, trendy shoulder bags, granny square bags, mesh totes, crossbody bags, and an everyday hobo bag.

Crochet bags are some of the most satisfying projects to make because they combine style with practicality. Unlike a decorative project that stays at home, a handmade bag can become part of your everyday wardrobe. You can use one for shopping, summer trips, carrying your crochet supplies, heading to the beach, or simply completing an outfit.

There is plenty of variety in this collection, too. Beginners can start with simple constructions such as the folded-rectangle crossbody bag, while crocheters looking for something different can experiment with bobble stitches, bean stitches, tapestry crochet, granny squares, gingham designs, and open mesh.

Many of these patterns also include video tutorials, making them helpful choices when you prefer to see each step demonstrated.

Whether you’re searching for an easy crochet bag pattern for beginners, a colorful granny square tote, or a modern crochet shoulder bag, here are 15 patterns worth saving.

 

1. Everyday Crochet Hobo Bag

 

The Everyday Crochet Hobo Bag is an excellent choice if you love relaxed, slouchy bags that work with casual outfits. The design uses a streamlined construction with minimal sewing, and the finished bag has integrated straps that create its characteristic hobo shape. The original pattern also provides guidance for adjusting the size, making it easy to customize the bag to suit your everyday essentials.

This is the kind of handmade accessory that could easily become your go-to bag for running errands, meeting friends, or carrying a few essentials while still giving your outfit that unmistakable crochet texture.

View the Free Everyday Crochet Hobo Bag Pattern →

2. Chunky Crochet Mesh Tote Bag

 

If you enjoy fast crochet projects, this Chunky Crochet Mesh Tote Bag deserves a spot high on your list. The chunky yarn and open mesh construction allow the project to work up quickly—the designer notes that the bag can be made in around two hours. It uses an oval-style base, mesh body, and crocheted straps to create a casual summer tote.

The breathable mesh design makes this crochet tote especially appealing for warm-weather outfits, trips to the beach, farmer’s markets, or casual shopping days. Try a soft neutral for a minimalist look or choose a bold yarn color to turn your handmade tote into the focal point of your outfit.

View the Free Chunky Crochet Mesh Tote Bag Pattern →

3. Mesh Crochet Tote Bag

 

A classic crochet mesh tote bag is one of those projects that can be used again and again. This version features a simple mesh design that works for different crochet skill levels, and the original pattern includes options for adjusting both the color and size.

Mesh crochet creates a lightweight fabric while still giving the bag plenty of visual texture. Use this tote for everyday errands, casual shopping, or as a reusable alternative to disposable bags. You can also experiment with seasonal colors to make several versions for different outfits.

View the Free Mesh Crochet Tote Bag Pattern →

4. Crochet Crescent Bag

 

 

Crescent bags have a curved silhouette that gives them a modern, fashion-forward appearance, and this Crochet Crescent Bag brings that popular shape into a handmade crochet project.

The finished bag can be worn over the shoulder or across the body, giving you multiple styling options. The pattern also includes instructions for adapting the size, so you can make a smaller accessory bag or a roomier everyday version depending on your preference.

If you have been looking for a trendy crochet crossbody bag pattern, this one offers an interesting alternative to the traditional rectangular bag.

View the Free Crochet Crescent Bag Pattern →

5. Granny Square Bag

 

 

A crochet granny square bag is a fun way to combine classic crochet with modern accessories. This clever design uses only three granny squares to create the bag, making it highly customizable in both size and color.

Granny square projects are also perfect for experimenting with leftover yarn. Make each square in a different color for a playful scrap-yarn bag, use two coordinating colors for a more polished look, or crochet everything in one neutral shade for a minimalist interpretation of the granny square trend.

Because you can control the size of the individual squares, the same basic idea can be adapted into anything from a small shoulder bag to a larger everyday crochet bag.

View the Free Granny Square Bag Pattern →

6. Crochet Bobble Bag

 

Texture makes handmade crochet accessories stand out, and the Crochet Bobble Bag delivers plenty of it. This pattern creates a slouchy bag using bobble-style stitches, giving the surface a dimensional appearance that immediately catches the eye.

The bag is crocheted primarily in one piece with only a small amount of sewing, and the original instructions explain how the size can be adjusted if you prefer something larger or smaller.

Choose a single yarn color to let the bobble texture do all the talking, or use a brighter shade if you want a statement crochet shoulder bag.

View the Free Crochet Bobble Bag Pattern →

7. Crochet Granny Stitch Tote Bag

 

If you love the appearance of granny squares but prefer a more continuous construction, try this Crochet Granny Stitch Tote Bag.

The familiar granny-style clusters create an open, textured fabric while the tote silhouette keeps the finished project practical. The design is intended as a functional everyday bag and comes with both a written pattern and a video tutorial.

This would look beautiful in classic cream, warm autumn shades, colorful stripes, or several contrasting yarn colors. It is an especially appealing project for anyone searching for a granny stitch crochet bag pattern with an everyday shape.

View the Free Crochet Granny Stitch Tote Bag Pattern →

8. Gingham Crochet Tote Bag

 

Gingham isn’t just for fabric. This Gingham Crochet Tote Bag recreates the familiar checked design with crochet colorwork, creating a striking handmade accessory.

One particularly appealing feature is its construction: the bag is crocheted in one piece with no sewing and relatively few loose ends. The same basic pattern can also be customized into gingham, checks, stripes, or even a solid-color tote.

Try classic black and white, soft pastel checks, brown and cream, or bright contrasting colors. Because the color combinations can completely change the appearance, this is one crochet tote bag pattern you could easily make more than once.

View the Free Gingham Crochet Tote Bag Pattern →

9. Simple Crochet Shoulder Bag

 

Sometimes a clean and simple design is exactly what you need. This Simple Crochet Shoulder Bag has an uncomplicated silhouette that makes it easy to pair with different outfits.

The bag is worked in one piece with very little sewing. The designer categorizes it as an advanced beginner project because one main stitch is used throughout, with just a small amount of decreasing required to shape the straps. Its height and strap length can also be adjusted.

If you’re searching for an easy crochet shoulder bag pattern, this is a great project to consider before moving on to more complicated colorwork or textured stitches.

View the Free Simple Crochet Shoulder Bag Pattern →

10. Flower Granny Square Tote Bag

 

Bring a little floral style to your crochet collection with this Flower Granny Square Tote Bag.

The tote is assembled from 13 granny squares and finished with a basic crocheted strap. Although flower granny squares are used in the original example, the same assembly method can work with other granny square designs, giving you plenty of opportunities to customize your bag.

This makes the project especially useful if you already have a favorite granny square motif. Try daisies for a cheerful spring bag, sunflower squares for summer, or traditional multicolor granny squares for a retro-inspired accessory.

View the Free Flower Granny Square Tote Bag Pattern →

11. Textured Crochet Shoulder Bag

 

If you want to learn a new stitch while making something useful, take a look at this Textured Crochet Shoulder Bag.

The pattern uses the bean stitch to create its distinctive texture, while the strap uses beginner-friendly single crochet. The designer recommends the project for advanced beginners, particularly because maintaining consistent tension with the bean stitch may take a little practice.

The result is a compact, highly textured shoulder bag that looks especially attractive in solid colors because the stitch definition remains the star of the design.

View the Free Textured Crochet Shoulder Bag Pattern →

12. Checkered Crochet Shoulder Bag

 

 

Checkerboard crochet is a great way to add bold pattern and contrast to a relatively simple bag shape.

This Checkered Crochet Shoulder Bag is crocheted in one piece with minimal sewing, while tapestry crochet is used to produce the repeating color pattern. The project mainly uses one stitch, but because yarn is carried while changing colors, it is particularly suited to advanced beginners ready to practice colorwork.

The possibilities for customization are nearly endless. Try black and white for a graphic look, brown and cream for a more neutral bag, or use pink, green, orange, blue, or another bold combination for a playful handmade accessory.

View the Free Checkered Crochet Shoulder Bag Pattern →

13. Easy Folded-Rectangle Crochet Crossbody Bag

 

 

Don’t let the interesting shape fool you—this is one of the simplest crochet bag constructions in the collection.

The Easy Folded-Rectangle Crossbody Bag begins as a single crocheted rectangle. The rectangle is then folded and sewn to create the finished bag shape. Even better for beginners, the pattern uses double crochet throughout.

The finished design can work as a crossbody bag, shoulder bag, or handbag depending on the strap length. Its clever folded construction makes it an excellent choice if you’re looking for your first crochet bag pattern but still want something that looks more interesting than a basic rectangle.

View the Free Easy Crochet Crossbody Bag Pattern →

14. Crochet Mini Shoulder Bag

 

 

Small bags have become a fun way to add a handmade detail to an outfit without carrying a large tote. This Crochet Mini Shoulder Bag, also described as a baguette-style bag, has a compact silhouette perfect for carrying a few essentials.

The project uses half double crochet throughout and is worked in rounds. The designer describes it as slightly beyond absolute-beginner level because working in rounds and attaching the strap may require a little additional confidence. The sample bag measures approximately 9 inches wide by 5.5 inches tall.

Make it in a neutral shade for a versatile everyday accessory or choose a bright statement color for a fun addition to your wardrobe.

View the Free Crochet Mini Shoulder Bag Pattern →

15. Crochet Mesh Tote Bag

 

 

We’ll finish the collection with another versatile crochet mesh tote bag, but this design offers a different construction from the earlier mesh options.

The bag is crocheted in one piece, beginning with an oval base before moving into the body and straps. Its mesh is intentionally not extremely open, helping smaller belongings stay more contained while still creating the light, airy appearance people love about mesh bags. The size is also adjustable.

A bag like this is ideal for summer. Use it as a crochet beach bag, farmer’s market tote, picnic bag, reusable shopping bag, or casual everyday carryall.

View the Free Crochet Mesh Tote Bag Pattern →

Photo Credit: The images shown in this tutorial are sourced from vivcrochets.com

Which Crochet Bag Pattern Should You Make First?

With so many different free crochet bag patterns available, choosing the first one may be the hardest part.

If you’re new to crochet bags, the folded-rectangle crossbody bag is an excellent place to begin because its construction starts with a simple rectangle and uses basic double crochet. The simple shoulder and mini shoulder bags are also approachable options once you’re comfortable working in rounds and shaping.

For something colorful, try the granny square bag, flower granny square tote, gingham tote, or checkered shoulder bag. These designs offer plenty of opportunities to experiment with different yarn combinations.

If texture is what catches your eye, the bobble bag and bean-stitch textured shoulder bag give you interesting stitch patterns to practice.

And for warm-weather projects, it’s hard to beat a crochet mesh tote bag. The open construction makes mesh totes lightweight and gives them that relaxed handmade style that works so well for summer.

Crochet Bag Ideas for Every Style

One of the best things about crocheting your own accessories is the freedom to make them match your personal style.

A single crochet bag pattern can look completely different depending on your yarn and color choices. Cream, beige, brown, and black create versatile neutral accessories, while bright pink, orange, green, or blue yarn can turn the exact same design into a statement piece.

You can also use your favorite color combinations to recreate current bag trends in a handmade way. Think colorful granny squares, checkerboard patterns, textured shoulder bags, slouchy hobo bags, minimalist crescent bags, and roomy market totes.

And because bags generally require less yarn than large garments, they can be great projects for testing new stitches and color combinations before committing to a sweater or cardigan.

Save These Free Crochet Bag Patterns for Later

Whether you want a roomy tote for shopping, a small shoulder bag for everyday essentials, a trendy crossbody bag, or a colorful granny square project, this collection offers plenty of inspiration for your next crochet project.

Save your favorite free crochet bag patterns so you can come back whenever you’re ready to pick up your hook and start another handmade accessory.

Happy crocheting! ♡

title.rendered: Basic Beaded Bracelet Tutorial: How to Make a Leather and Bead Wrap Bracelet

content.rendered:
A basic beaded bracelet is a great project if you want to combine simple leather cord with colorful beads for a handmade bracelet that looks much more complicated than it really is.

This tutorial shows you how to make a leather and bead wrap bracelet using round leather cord, beading thread, a metal button, and a mix of fire-polished and magatama beads. The finished bracelet wraps around the wrist multiple times and closes with a simple button-and-loop clasp.

It is a good project for beginners who already feel comfortable using a needle and thread and want to try a more polished beaded jewelry design.

Pattern credit: Chris Franchetti Michaels.

What You’ll Need

Tools

  • Measuring tape
  • Side cutters or flush cutters
  • Clipboard
  • Size 10 beading needle
  • Masking tape or painter’s tape
  • Thread burner
  • Scissors, optional

Materials

  • 72 inches of 2 mm round leather cord
  • One 17 mm round metal button
  • Beading thread, 6-pound tensile strength
  • 45 fire-polished glass beads, 4 mm
    • 15 color A
    • 15 color B
    • 15 color C
  • 30 magatama beads, 3 mm
    • 15 color D
    • 15 color E
  • About 6 inches of C-Lon beading cord, optional

These are the materials and tools specified in the source tutorial.

How to Make a Leather and Bead Wrap Bracelet

Step 1: Measure and Cut the Leather Cord

Start by wrapping a measuring tape around your wrist as many times as you want the finished bracelet to wrap.

Keep the tape a little looser than the final fit you want because the beads will add thickness.

For the sample bracelet, the wrist measurement was 24 inches.

Add 12 inches to your measurement, then double the result.

For example:

  • Wrist measurement: 24 inches
  • 24 + 12 = 36 inches
  • 36 × 2 = 72 inches

Cut the leather cord to that length using side cutters.

Step 2: String the Button

Take your metal button and thread the leather cord up through one hole and down through the second hole.

Slide the button until it sits at the center of the cord.

The two leather ends should now be approximately equal in length.

Step 3: Secure the Cord and Begin the Thread

Clamp the button end of the leather cord under the clip of your clipboard.

Cut a long piece of bead thread, at least about two arm spans.

Thread the beading needle so the needle sits near the middle of the thread, creating a double strand.

Bring the loose thread ends together and tie them loosely around one strand of leather cord close to the clipboard clip.

Leave at least 8 inches of thread tail so you can weave the ends into the beadwork later.

If you are right-handed, it may be easier to tie the thread to the left leather strand; if left-handed, use the right strand.

Tape the loose thread tails down to keep them out of the way.

Step 4: String and Position the First Bead

 

Pick up one color A bead with the needle.

Slide it all the way down the thread.

Pass the needle underneath both leather cords.

Use your finger to push the bead upward so it sits neatly between the two leather strands.

Step 5: Stitch the First Bead

 

 

Pass the needle back through the same bead, this time going over the top of both leather cords.

Hold the bead in place with your fingers while pulling the thread snug.

Pull slowly.

Because you are working with double thread, make sure both strands tighten evenly around the leather.

If the thread begins to tangle, stop and straighten it before continuing.

Step 6: Slide the First Bead Into Place

Gently slide the first bead closer to the clipboard clip.

The first few beads should sit relatively close to the button.

This keeps the beginning of the beadwork neat and reduces unnecessary gaps near the clasp.

 

Step 7: String the Second Bead

Pick up one color B bead.

Slide it down the thread.

Pass the needle underneath both leather cords again.

Push the bead upward so it fits between the cords beside the first bead.

 

Step 8: Make the Second Stitch

Pass the needle back through the second bead.

Pull the thread tight slowly, just as you did with the first bead.

Keep the bead centered between the leather cords and maintain even tension.

 

 

Step 9: Stitch the Third Bead

Pick up one color C bead.

Use the same technique:

  • slide the bead down the thread
  • pass beneath the leather cords
  • position the bead between them
  • pass back through the bead
  • pull the thread snug

You now have the first A-B-C color sequence.

 

 

Step 10: Keep Stitching Beads

Continue building the pattern.

Add another sequence of:

  • one color A bead
  • one color B bead
  • one color C bead

Then add three color D magatama beads together, treating the group as if it were one bead.

Next, stitch:

  • two more A-B-C sequences
  • three color E magatama beads together

Keep alternating these bead sequences.

The source tutorial recommends stopping with a fire-polished bead when you have about 8 inches of thread remaining.

The sample bracelet reached around 9 inches of beadwork before a new thread was needed.

 

Keeping the Bead Pattern Even

As you work, check that the beads remain centered between the leather strands.

Try to maintain consistent thread tension.

Too loose, and the beads may shift.

Too tight, and the leather may begin to pinch inward.

Take your time and correct the placement as you go.

Step 11: End the Old Thread

When your working thread becomes too short, weave it back into the bracelet before starting a new strand.

Turn the beadwork over.

Pass the needle back through the last bead you stitched.

Make a small loop with the thread and pass the needle through it to create a securing knot.

Turn the bracelet right-side up and pass back through the bead.

Turn it again and pass through the bead from the back.

Repeat once more so the thread is woven securely into the beadwork.

Use a thread burner to trim the thread close to where it exits the bead.

Also remove the excess thread that was originally tied around the leather cord.

 

 

Step 12: Start a New Thread

Cut a fresh length of beading thread.

Attach it to the leather cord the same way you did at the beginning.

Thread your needle and continue adding beads from the point where you stopped.

 

Step 13: Complete the Beading

Continue adding beads until the bracelet reaches the length you want.

Start a new thread whenever necessary.

When the beadwork is complete, weave in the final thread tails using the same method used earlier.

Make sure all thread ends are secure before moving on to the clasp.

 

How Long Should a Leather Wrap Bracelet Be?

The ideal length depends on:

  • wrist size
  • number of wraps
  • bead size
  • preferred fit

The best approach is to test the bracelet around your wrist as you work.

Stop when the beadwork wraps comfortably without feeling too tight.

Step 14: Tie the End Knots

At the end opposite the button, tie an overhand knot using both leather cords.

Position it close to the last bead.

Pull it tight.

Next, use the button itself as your measuring guide.

Tie a second overhand knot so the space between the two knots is slightly longer than the button diameter.

Test the button in the loop before tightening the second knot fully.

This creates the bracelet’s button-and-loop clasp.

 

 

Step 15: Optional — Wrap C-Lon Cord Below the Button

For a cleaner finish, you can wrap a short piece of C-Lon beading cord around both leather strands directly beneath the button.

Wrap it several times.

Tie it securely.

Trim the ends with scissors.

This step is optional, but it can help keep the button stable and give the bracelet a more finished appearance.

 

 

Step 16: Finish the Leather and Bead Wrap Bracelet

Use side cutters to trim the two leather tails.

Leave at least 1 inch of leather beyond the second knot on the loop end.

Check the clasp one final time.

The button should pass through the leather loop securely but still be easy enough to open when needed.

Your leather and bead wrap bracelet is now ready to wear.

 

 

Tips for a Neat Beaded Wrap Bracelet

Keep the Leather Parallel

Try to keep the two leather strands evenly spaced while stitching.

This helps the bracelet maintain a consistent width.

Pull the Thread Slowly

Fast pulling makes tangles more likely.

Slow, controlled tension gives you cleaner bead placement.

Check the Fit Before Finishing

Wrap the bracelet around your wrist before tying the final closure knots.

That is much easier than trying to adjust the length after everything is finished.

Keep the Button Loop Snug

The loop should be large enough for the button to pass through, but not so large that it slips open easily.

Bead Color Ideas

The original pattern uses five bead colors, but you can adapt the color palette.

Try combinations such as:

  • turquoise, cream, and bronze
  • black, silver, and gray
  • blush pink, ivory, and gold
  • navy, white, and copper
  • green, amber, and brown
  • rainbow colors
  • neutral earth tones

You can also use only two or three colors for a simpler look.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is this leather and bead bracelet beginner-friendly?

Yes, but it is slightly more advanced than a simple cord bracelet because it involves a beading needle and thread.

It is still approachable if you work slowly and follow the bead-stitching sequence carefully.

What size leather cord is used?

The source pattern uses 2 mm round leather cord.

What size beads are used?

The bracelet uses:

  • 4 mm fire-polished glass beads
  • 3 mm magatama beads

How does the bracelet close?

A metal button is attached at one end.

Two overhand knots create a leather loop at the opposite end, forming a simple button-and-loop clasp.

What should I do when the bead thread runs out?

Weave the thread back through the final bead, secure it, trim it, and attach a new thread to the leather cord.

Then continue beading from where you stopped.

Can I change the bead pattern?

Yes.

The original design uses repeating fire-polished bead sequences with groups of magatama beads, but you can customize the color order as long as the beads fit comfortably between the leather strands.

Quick Pattern Summary

  1. Measure your wrist and calculate the leather length.
  2. Cut the leather cord.
  3. Center the button on the cord.
  4. Secure the leather to a clipboard.
  5. Tie on the bead thread.
  6. Add the first bead.
  7. Stitch through it.
  8. Add the second bead.
  9. Add the third bead.
  10. Continue the repeating bead pattern.
  11. Weave in the old thread.
  12. Start a new thread.
  13. Continue until the bracelet reaches the desired length.
  14. Tie the leather loop closure.
  15. Add optional C-Lon wrapping under the button.
  16. Trim the leather ends and finish the bracelet.

Make Your Own Basic Beaded Bracelet

This basic beaded bracelet is a beautiful next step if you want to move beyond simple knotting patterns and try a bracelet that combines leather, beads, and hand stitching.

The leather gives the bracelet structure, while the beads add color and texture. The button closure also gives the finished piece a handmade jewelry look without requiring a metal clasp.

Once you understand the basic stitching method, you can customize the bracelet with your own bead colors, wrap length, button style, and bead sequence.

Pattern credit: Chris Franchetti Michaels.
